To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nanofilled and nanostructured epoxides are promising candidates to replace the traditional epoxy resins in a wide range of applications.

epoxy nanocomposites are a class of advanced materials, which can be tailored to meet the requirements of specific applications, by the proper choice of the nanofiller, of the method of dispersion, and of the curing conditions, and that their properties can be improved in comparison to the pristine epoxy resin.
the nanofilled and nanostructured epoxides have a great potential for applications in many fields of science and technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of novel epoxy nanocomposites with improved properties, in terms of mechanical, electrical, thermal, and optical, for applications such as structural materials, coatings, and electronics.
developing novel nanostructures for applications in the field of nanomedicine and nanobiotechnology.

the preparation and characterization of nanofilled epoxy systems and the investigation of their potential applications in the field of adhesives, coatings, and composite materials for the aerospace industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future for the development of nanocomposites based upon epoxies is very promising, especially for the applications in which the mechanical and thermal performances are the key factors.
the use of epoxy nanocomposite materials in many fields is a reality, and that their future is promising, especially if the nanofillering is combined with the nanostructuring of the epoxy matrix.

the nanotechnology has opened new horizons to the epoxy-based nanocomposites, allowing them to compete with other polymeric materials in many applications, and in particular, in those requiring a combination of high mechanical properties and high electrical and thermal performances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of nanofilled and nanostructured epoxymers has been widely explored in the last few years, but their full potential has not been fully exploited yet.
the use of nanoparticles as fillers in epoxy matrices has opened new horizons in the development of new materials with improved properties.
the use of nanofillers and the development of new nanocomposites based upon epoxy resin are a promising approach for the development of new materials with improved performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epoxy nanocomposites represent a new class of materials that can be tailored to satisfy a broad range of requirements, and their potential is not fully exploited.
the epoxy nanocomposites can be considered as the most promising materials to replace conventional polymers in the future.
the nanofilled/nanoparticle-filled epoxies are a class of materials that are able to combine the advantages of both organic and inorganic materials.
